outcome: Eyal Markman proved the Hodge conjecture for abelian varieties of complex dimension 4 and (in a companion result) 5, a genuine human-authored case of the conjecture, digested by experts via a dedicated two-day seminar series and a September 2026 guest post by Burt Totaro on Terence Tao's blog. Separately, a cluster of low-credibility arXiv preprints (K3 surfaces, complete intersections, Calabi-Yau 5-folds, 'spectral rigidity' frameworks) claimed full or partial proofs; one was withdrawn by arXiv admin for policy violation, one was withdrawn and resubmitted by its own author without explanation, and none has been endorsed by any expert. An anonymously-sourced media report claims OpenAI is close to an internal solution, but as of the report date no paper, code, or Clay Institute statement exists.
credited_humans: Jonathan Pridham (2024 semi-regularity extension used as a key input)

disputes.summary: A wave of 2025 arXiv preprints (e.g. arXiv:2507.18999 'Constructive Proof of the Hodge Conjecture for K3 Surfaces via Nodal Degenerations'; arXiv:2507.09934 on complete intersections; arXiv:2507.12173 'Spectral Rigidity and Algebraicity'; arXiv:2506.17754 on Calabi-Yau 5-folds) claim proofs or frameworks for the full or restricted Hodge conjecture. arXiv:2507.12173 was withdrawn by arXiv Admin for 'violation of arXiv policies for acceptable submissions' (no further detail given) after a v1-to-v2 collapse from 7KB to 1KB; arXiv:2506.17754 was withdrawn by its own author and silently resubmitted days later with no explanation. None of these has any expert digestion, citation, or endorsement found; their titles and abstracts (invoking ad hoc 'spectral fingerprints', 'exceptional group constraints', etc.) match a pattern of low-quality or likely AI-generated preprints that surfaced across arXiv math sections in 2025-2026 and prompted community and moderator concern (arXiv's October 2025 restriction on AI-heavy survey/review submissions, and Terence Tao's and others' public commentary on a 'crisis of AI-generated mathematics'). No source establishes that these specific Hodge preprints were AI-authored; this is treated as unresolved and non-credible rather than as a confirmed AI claim.

The Information reported (17 September 2026), citing anonymous sources, that OpenAI is 'close to solving' the Hodge conjecture as a second Millennium Prize problem, following its disputed 8 September 2026 Navier-Stokes announcement. OpenAI itself has only said it made 'substantial progress' on an unnamed Millennium problem; the Hodge Conjecture attribution originated in a viral, since-controversial X post (9 September 2026) rather than from OpenAI. As of the most recent sources checked (around 17-22 September 2026), there is no paper, no code, and no Clay Mathematics Institute statement regarding the Hodge conjecture from OpenAI.

summary: The only credible movement on the Hodge conjecture since 26 January 2024 is Eyal Markman's proof, posted to arXiv on 5 February 2025 (arXiv:2502.03415, 'Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds', v2 8 June 2025), that the Hodge conjecture holds for all abelian fourfolds (and, per follow-up work, fivefolds) of Weil type, hence for all abelian fourfolds. This is a case of the stated problem under §3.1 (restricting to abelian varieties of low dimension), not a resolution of the general conjecture, so status is 'partial' with resolution_direction 'confirmed'. It has real expert digestion: a dedicated two-day seminar series ('The Hodge Conjecture for Abelian Fourfolds, after Markman') worked through the proof section by section, and Burt Totaro's guest post on Terence Tao's blog (11 September 2026) describes it in detail as a genuine breakthrough building on Ben Moonen-Yuri Zarhin's 1995 reduction and Jonathan Pridham's 2024 extension of Buchweitz-Flenner semi-regularity theory to twisted sheaves. No AI system is credited anywhere in this work; it is entirely human-authored classical algebraic geometry, so ai_role is 'none'. Separately, I found a cluster of 2025 arXiv preprints purporting much stronger results (full proofs for K3 surfaces, complete intersections, or general frameworks), none of which show any sign of expert acceptance, citation, or even engagement; one (2507.12173) was pulled by arXiv Admin itself for a policy violation, and another (2506.17754, Calabi-Yau 5-folds) was withdrawn and quietly resubmitted by its sole author. These match a broader, well-documented pattern of low-quality/AI-assisted preprint spam on arXiv math sections in 2025-2026 (prompting arXiv's October 2025 restriction on survey/review papers and public commentary, including Tao's, on a 'crisis of AI-generated mathematics'), but I found no source that specifically confirms these Hodge preprints were AI-generated, so I record them as a credibility dispute rather than an AI claim, and they do not change the problem's status. Finally, there is an active but entirely unconfirmed media story: The Information reported (17 September 2026, anonymous sources) that OpenAI is close to an internal solution of the Hodge conjecture, as a second Millennium Prize problem after its disputed Navier-Stokes claim of 8 September 2026. This traces to a viral X post naming Hodge specifically; OpenAI's own public statement names no specific problem. No paper, code, or Clay Institute statement exists for Hodge from OpenAI as of the most recent reporting I could check (around 17-22 September 2026), so under §6.1/§6.2 this cannot be coded as claimed or generated — it is not evidence of any change to the problem, only a rumor, and does not affect status.
competing_reading: One could argue the low-quality preprint cluster and/or the OpenAI rumor deserve a 'claimed' status with ai_role 'incident', on the theory that an AI-produced claim was effectively 'announced' via leaks and social media even without a formal paper. I rejected this because §6.1 requires a preprint, announcement, or machine-checked certificate for 'claimed', and neither OpenAI nor any credible author has actually claimed a Hodge conjecture proof in a citable, attributable document as of my research; the only announced OpenAI Millennium claim with a real paper is Navier-Stokes, a different problem. If OpenAI (or another lab) publishes an actual paper or technical report naming the Hodge conjecture, this record would need to move to 'claimed' or 'progress'/'incident' depending on outcome.
what_would_settle_it: A citable OpenAI (or other lab) paper, technical report, or system card explicitly naming the Hodge conjecture with a claimed result, which does not yet exist; or expert commentary (e.g. from Totaro, Tao, or other algebraic geometers) explicitly addressing and dismissing or confirming any of the 2025 arXiv preprint cluster, which I did not find.

judgement.doubts: Agree with the record. Markman's result is a case (abelian fourfolds) of the general conjecture, digested via a dedicated seminar and Totaro's named guest post on Tao's blog. The fivefold extension is mentioned only vaguely ('per follow-up work') and is not separately sourced; it does not affect the code.
